messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] read.transcript.features when BED file is an object
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] read.transcript.features when BED file is an object
messages.body_plain:
One possible way is
Write down the subset p2 as a bed file (rtracklayer package will help you in exporting dataframe to bed file)
read the bed file back into methylKit using read.transcript.features

Other possible way is to subset a transcript features file read in methylkit (not sure if this works, but I would try to check)
read a bed file using read.transcript.features
read the list of genes/transcript names as a vector/dataframe.
filter like this
P.obj[P.obj$exons$name==plus], where P.obj is an object obtained from read.transcript.features and plus is a df (of interested genes/transcript names)

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.subject: annotate.WithGenicParts selection of transcript overlap
messages.subject_clean: annotate.WithGenicParts selection of transcript overlap
messages.body_plain:
Dear discussion group,

I would like to gain a better understanding of how the “annotate.WithGenicParts” function works (in relation to getting the distance to the nearest TSS).

My issue is that I have used region counts to generate regions across the genome that are 600 bases in length:

gene500.obj=read.transcript.features("hg19.EnsemblGenes.bed",up.flank=500,down.flank=100)

Tss500=regionCounts(myobj2,gene500.obj$promoters,cov.bases=10,strand.aware=TRUE)

However, some regions are annotated to the same transcript ID when in theory, there should only be one region per transcript ID.

My suspicion is that “annotate.With.GenicParts” annotates the first instance of overlap, not considering all overlapping region Transcript possibilities; as there seems to only be a 1-to-1 match for each region to each transcript.

Below is a region defined in:

prom<-as.data.frame(gene500.obj$promoters)

head(prom)

seqnames    start      end width strand score name

1     chr1 66998565 66999165   601      +     0    .

This particular region is specific to TSS(1) where

TSS(1), TSS(2) and TSS(3) start at:

66999065=TSS(1) start

66998765=TSS(2) start

66999100=TSS(3) start

All 3 of these TSS overlap with the region shown in (prom).

How does “annotate.WithGenicParts” choose the correct TSS (1,2 or3) when all 3 TSS overlap with the region provided?  I specifically would like to see “annotate.WithGenicParts” to call it an overlap when the TSS of the transcript is starting ~base 500 of my 600 base region; would it be possible to force the command to consider where the overlap occurs?

Thanks,

Michelle

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Altuna,

I can imagine how frustrating it can be for you to diagnose a problem when users' questions are not clear enough. Providing a "reproducable" code, however, can  be tricky. With my little knowledge of R I have been spending sleepless nights to diagnose the problem as well. My post below might not be "reproducable" but I believe it might give you some clue on the cause of the problem. This is the codes I run:

myobj.3 =read( file.list.3, pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE, chr.col=1, start.col=2, end.col=2, coverage.col=6, strand.col=3, freqC.col=5 ),
               sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("Neo-intimal SMC", "BMMC", "PBMC"), assembly="rn5", treatment=c(1,0, 0), context="CpG")

# get tiling window
tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
# calculate differential methylation from tile window
myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25)

The interesting thing I find is that the "chr" set in myDiff25p.3 and get.res are not necessarily the same. I have exported them into a csv files below for your perusal:

myDiff25p.3
https://www.dropbox.com/s/m77tg0owkpo4jag/test-diff-meth-25p.txt?dl=0

and

get.res(i.e., diffMethPerChr)
https://www.dropbox.com/s/lhs28lowa317yep/test-diff-meth-per-chr.txt?dl=0

I wonder where the "chr*random" are coming from. Are the methods using different versions of the reference genome(i.e., rn5)?

Thanks a lot for your patience.

messages.body_plain:
Altuna,

I profusely apologize for all the trouble this might be causing; my project has stalled. Sending a Reproducible example in this kind of work is not clear and very tricky with this kind of work. I hope you won't mind a reproducible snippet of my r code and a link to my meth.ratio data. Maybe, maybe, that might help. I am very sorry once again for going this route!

links to my data:

https://www.dropbox.com/s/4hdrpxwzmjp1t2z/sample_B.txt?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/kuhvbcjbrectatx/sample_C.txt?dl=0
https://www.dropbox.com/s/p286v9mnb1yhc51/sample_D.txt?dl=0

This is my r code:

# Load required packages
library(methylKit)

sample.b <- "~/sample_B.txt"
sample.c <- "~/sample_C.txt"
sample.d <- "~/sample_D.txt"

# create file list and process data
file.list <- list(sample.b, sample.c, sample.d)

# create object from samples
myobj =read(file.list, pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE, chr.col=1, start.col=2, end.col=2, coverage.col=6, strand.col=3, freqC.col=5 ),
               sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("Sample B", "Sample C", "Sample D"), assembly="rn5", treatment=c(1,0, 0), context="CpG")

# get tiling window
tiles=tileMethylCounts(myobj, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
meth.tile=unite(tiles, destrand=TRUE)

# calculate differential methylation from tile window

myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth.tile, num.cores=2)

You will find the vignette for methylkit clarify all the points raised by you.   Also, try '?read' you will get well documented explanation about the read() function.

methylkit package website also has tutorial how to read files!

Regards,
Kalyan

On 7 October 2014 21:27, <alejandro...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi
> I'm reading four files (duplicates for genotype C and duplicates for genotype B), see below.
>
> > comparisonName="C_ctrl_vs_B_ctrol_unite_filter_compare";

> > B1=paste(B4_ctrl, chrom, "MethylKit.inputdata.CpG.txt", sep=".");

> Ale

You have read it what it means. A 'string' is a 'character' it doesn't need to be a file. A 'string' is stored as such!

methylKit don't need a file. Infact, by assigning 'TAIR10' you are simply telling it that you have aligned your data with a genome named 'TAIR10'. At no point methylkit require the actual 'TAIR10' genome.

It is worth to go through the definition of terms in R!

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs from Tiling window and "diffMethPerChr"

messages.body_plain:
still not good enough, I'm afraid :/, it requires a lot of work on my part to read csv files and convert them to methylKit objects, I'm doing this on my spare time and have a really busy schedule. The less work it requires, the quicker I can help. Ideally what I mean by a reproducible example is that you should save the subset of the methylKit objects  in rdata format with saveRDS(), and send along the code that reads that file, runs the commands and reproduces the problem.

But I think your problems seems to be the * _random chromosomes. I can't tell at what point they enter your analysis, but I think you can ignore them, as it seems they don't have any differential methylation. Just subset your methylBase or methylDiff object with pattern matching using grep, sth like the following might work

meth.3.tile[grep("_random|chrUn",meth.3.tile$chr,invert=TRUE),]

In your case I would also suggest the following: you can try to pool your samples, you have no replicates for one of the conditions, pooling will enable you to compare conditions when there is no replicate for one of them and make sure you use the appropriate coverage thresholds, even though you can didn't get an error before it doesn't mean your results are reliable with 1X coverage.
http://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methylKit/functions/pool-methods

tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
meth.3.tile=pool(meth.3.tile,sample.ids=c("test","control") )

myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25)

messages.body_plain:
can you try what I suggested earlier here as well, remove the _random and chrUn chromosomes, also pool your data. This might resolve your problem. If you want more help, you can try saving "meth.tile"  with saveRDS() and share that instead. But please try the suggestions first. I think you have low coverage data and no replicates for one of the conditions, so that it self might create a problem. If you use pool() you might be able to get something.

Best,
Altuna

Thanks a lot! I get what you expect for reproducible example now. I will try your suggestions and get back to you. I honestly appreciate you help. Thanks once again!

On Tuesday, October 7, 2014 5:40:42 PM UTC-4, Altuna Akalin wrote:

> still not good enough, I'm afraid :/, it requires a lot of work on my part to read csv files and convert them to methylKit objects, I'm doing this on my spare time and have a really busy schedule. The less work it requires, the quicker I can help. Ideally what I mean by a reproducible example is that you should save the subset of the methylKit objects  in rdata format with saveRDS(), and send along the code that reads that file, runs the commands and reproduces the problem.
>
> But I think your problems seems to be the * _random chromosomes. I can't tell at what point they enter your analysis, but I think you can ignore them, as it seems they don't have any differential methylation. Just subset your methylBase or methylDiff object with pattern matching using grep, sth like the following might work
>
> meth.3.tile[grep("_random|chrUn",meth.3.tile$chr,invert=TRUE),]
>
> In your case I would also suggest the following: you can try to pool your samples, you have no replicates for one of the conditions, pooling will enable you to compare conditions when there is no replicate for one of them and make sure you use the appropriate coverage thresholds, even though you can didn't get an error before it doesn't mean your results are reliable with 1X coverage.
> http://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methylKit/functions/pool-methods
>
>
> tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
> meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
> meth.3.tile=pool(meth.3.tile,sample.ids=c("test","control") )
> myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
> myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
> get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25)
>

> On Tue, Oct 7, 2014 at 5:47 PM, Atongo <ato...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Thanks Altuna,
> >
> > I can imagine how frustrating it can be for you to diagnose a problem when users' questions are not clear enough. Providing a "reproducable" code, however, can  be tricky. With my little knowledge of R I have been spending sleepless nights to diagnose the problem as well. My post below might not be "reproducable" but I believe it might give you some clue on the cause of the problem. This is the codes I run:
> >
> > myobj.3 =read( file.list.3, pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE, chr.col=1, start.col=2, end.col=2, coverage.col=6, strand.col=3, freqC.col=5 ),
> >                sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("Neo-intimal SMC", "BMMC", "PBMC"), assembly="rn5", treatment=c(1,0, 0), context="CpG")
> >
> > # get tiling window
> > tiles.3=tileMethylCounts(myobj.3, win.size=1000,step.size=1000)
> > meth.3.tile=unite(tiles.3, destrand=TRUE)
> > # calculate differential methylation from tile window
> > myDiff.3=calculateDiffMeth(meth.3.tile, num.cores=2)
> > myDiff25p.3=get.methylDiff(myDiff.3, difference=25, qvalue=0.01)
> > get.res <- diffMethPerChr(myDiff.3, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25)
> >
> > The interesting thing I find is that the "chr" set in myDiff25p.3 and get.res are not necessarily the same. I have exported them into a csv files below for your perusal:
> >
> > myDiff25p.3
> > https://www.dropbox.com/s/m77tg0owkpo4jag/test-diff-meth-25p.txt?dl=0
> >
> > and
> >
> > get.res(i.e., diffMethPerChr)
> > https://www.dropbox.com/s/lhs28lowa317yep/test-diff-meth-per-chr.txt?dl=0
> >
> > I wonder where the "chr*random" are coming from. Are the methods using different versions of the reference genome(i.e., rn5)?
> >

> > Thanks a lot for your patience.
> >
> > On Monday, October 6, 2014 5:58:42 PM UTC-4, Altuna Akalin wrote:

> > > rows shouldn't have NaNs unless there was sth went wrong in the previous steps.
> > > You can subset the methylDiff object with [] notation like you would subset a data frame, but I suggest doing this only if you understand what went wrong in the previous steps.

> > > On Mon, Oct 6, 2014 at 10:54 PM, Atongo <ato...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > > I tried the "diffMethPerChr" from myDiff object from a tiling window. The figure was gabbled. I realized that some rows had a lot of "0" and "NaN". How can I eliminate these rows before plotting? Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Kalyan is right about the assembly argument, it is just a string so that users know what assembly is used in alignment process at any given time. AFAIR, It will also prohibit users using objects that have different assemblies in certain functions.

12 column BED file is needed for annotation (refer to vignette on how and where to use it) you don't need it if you don't need to annotate your DMRs/DMCs. Again, clear examples are all around on how that works: paper, vignette, this forum. Also search for TAIR10 in the forum, there were other people trying to use that assembly.

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] annotate.WithGenicParts selection of transcript overlap
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] annotate.WithGenicParts selection of transcript overlap
messages.body_plain:
If I understood correctly, there are 3 promoter regions which are coming from 3 close-by TSSes. To find the nearest TSS to DMRs/DMCs we use the nearest() function from IRanges with default arguments. Which means, when there is a tie, in your case  the promoter have 0 distance to all 3 TSSes, one of them will be picked arbitrarily.

You can not force the function to do what you want ,unfortunately.

Best,
Altuna

On Tue, Oct 7, 2014 at 12:28 PM, Michelle Johnson <md...@medschl.cam.ac.uk> wrote:

> Dear discussion group,
>
>
>
> I would like to gain a better understanding of how the “annotate.WithGenicParts” function works (in relation to getting the distance to the nearest TSS).
>
>
>
> My issue is that I have used region counts to generate regions across the genome that are 600 bases in length:
>
>
>
> gene500.obj=read.transcript.features("hg19.EnsemblGenes.bed",up.flank=500,down.flank=100)
>
> Tss500=regionCounts(myobj2,gene500.obj$promoters,cov.bases=10,strand.aware=TRUE)
>
>
>
> However, some regions are annotated to the same transcript ID when in theory, there should only be one region per transcript ID.
>
> My suspicion is that “annotate.With.GenicParts” annotates the first instance of overlap, not considering all overlapping region Transcript possibilities; as there seems to only be a 1-to-1 match for each region to each transcript.
>
>
>
> Below is a region defined in:
>
> prom<-as.data.frame(gene500.obj$promoters)
>
>
>
> head(prom)
>
> seqnames    start      end width strand score name
>
> 1     chr1 66998565 66999165   601      +     0    .
>
>
>
> This particular region is specific to TSS(1) where
>
> TSS(1), TSS(2) and TSS(3) start at:
>
>
>
> 66999065=TSS(1) start
>
> 66998765=TSS(2) start
>
> 66999100=TSS(3) start
>
>
>
> All 3 of these TSS overlap with the region shown in (prom).
>
>
>
> How does “annotate.WithGenicParts” choose the correct TSS (1,2 or3) when all 3 TSS overlap with the region provided?  I specifically would like to see “annotate.WithGenicParts” to call it an overlap when the TSS of the transcript is starting ~base 500 of my 600 base region; would it be possible to force the command to consider where the overlap occurs?
>
>
>

>
> Michelle

messages.body_plain:
Hi run this command in order to start the process of annotating my diff methylated CpGs

> gene.obj=read.transcript.features(file.path("/Users/acolaneri_2000/Documents/Jones_Lab/Methyl_seq_PEG/Final_analysis_after_resequencing/for_MethylKit","TAIR10"))

and I get this error.

Error in .Call2("solve_user_SEW0", start, end, width, PACKAGE = "IRanges") :
  solving row 85: negative widths are not allowed

Looking in the phoro I found this post, were Altuna is explaining a possible source for this type of error:

>From Altuna:  "I think the problem is in the file structure. Usually, Column 11 and 12 of the bed file contains the blockSizes and blockStarts which denote the start and length of each exon. What is out of ordinary about that file is that for "-" strand blockStarts do not start with 0 and the order of the start positions in the blockStarts column is reversed. Below is  an example. Where column 11 and column 12 is reversed for "-" strand.

> ref[ref$V4=="AT5G08160.1",]
    V1      V2      V3          V4 V5 V6      V7      V8 V9 V10
2 chr5 2625558 2628110 AT5G08160.1  0  - 2625902 2627942  0   6
                       V11                       V12
2 385,143,144,186,125,573, 2167,1523,1269,928,659,0,

column 11 should be:
573,125,186,144,143,385,

column 12 should be:
0,659,928,1269,1523,2167

You can pre-process (perl, awk, etc. ) the BED entries on "-" strand and reverse the order of values in column 11 and 12, and then it should work. The function which extracts the intron coordinates from the BED file, assumes such an order and that's why it throws an error where a GRanges object with negative width can not be created.

Best,
Altuna"

I was loking at my 12 column bed files and that does not appear to be my case.

chr1, 45295, 47019, AT1G01080, 0, -, 45502, 46789, 0, 4, 264,309,102,644, 0,350,748,1080,

* comas in red were put by my to indicate different columns

I do not know what can be wrong in my case.
I will appreciate help or suggestions
Ale

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] data import
messages.body_plain:
could you explain what exactly are you referring to when you say custom dataset/assembly? There is a way to read generic methylation ratio/percentage per base files? if that what you mean by custom dataset?

Assembly is dealt with upstream of methylKit, if you can align reads and call methylation, you can use that assembly. Only problem is that you need to have proper BED files for gene annotation when you want to annotate DMCs/DMRs. You can try to convert gff to bed, one way of doing that is the following:
http://www.raetschlab.org/suppl/gff-tools

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I glanced at your bed file. The first impression is that the file is not sorted (you may try sortBed from bedtools).

It seems you are trying to explore the methylation at the miRNAs. There is only one exon for every entry and no introns. So, this bed file is purely a list of exons and not actually transcripts of genes with features like exons, introns, cds, promoters! Since read.transcript.features() internally tries to extract introns and seems to get struck (I am not sure but this is may be a possible case).

If you could let us know further details of the objective, this forum might help!

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.body_plain:
sorting shouldn't matter actually. If you are getting that error, it means something is fundamentally wrong with the bed file or how it is interpreted by the functions. The file should be tab-separated and there should be 12 columns, 2nd and 3rd columns should be integer.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
Hi!

Sorry I am new in processing methylation data so my wording is certainly not the right one...

Actually, I have some 96 Phaseolus vulgaris individuals (6 different groups/varieties) and wanted to analyze them...
I prepare the bed files as shown in p3 of the manual... I will get the assembly form another team (who called the methylation)

What do you mean by "proper BED file for gene annotation"? Is there a description of the assembly file I could use as a reference...?

The manual mainly shows how to open data from the MethylKit package and is not really explicit about how to import your own data... Should I use the option "system.file" or just "list"?

Thanks for your help!!

Jonathan

Le jeudi 9 octobre 2014 15:22:37 UTC-4, Altuna Akalin a écrit :

> could you explain what exactly are you referring to when you say custom dataset/assembly? There is a way to read generic methylation ratio/percentage per base files? if that what you mean by custom dataset?
>
> Assembly is dealt with upstream of methylKit, if you can align reads and call methylation, you can use that assembly. Only problem is that you need to have proper BED files for gene annotation when you want to annotate DMCs/DMRs. You can try to convert gff to bed, one way of doing that is the following:
> http://www.raetschlab.org/suppl/gff-tools

messages.body_plain:
You have duplicated transcript ids that are mapping same TSS and TES. Normally, we expect that transcript ids are unique per transcript. At least in human and mouse certain transcripts map more than once, but to different locations in the genome. We can deal with those cases even though transcript ids are not unique, but not with the case exemplified below. In this case, same transcript maps to the same exact boundary but only couple of internal exons are different. You can try to make transcript ids unique by adding row number to the 4th column. so AT5G59090 becomes AT5G59090_2345 ( 2345 is the row number) and so on.

messages.body_plain:
The solution to this is a general R concept! Always a file or location or path needs to be defined in quotes. For example:

file.list=list("/path/of/file1","/path/of/file2".........). Also giving path depends on your OS (windows follows backslash).

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.body_plain:
You can do that as well, whichever is the easiest for you. For the annotation part, you can get a matrix per DMR/DMC showing overlap status with exons, introns, promoters etc. You don't get a list of DMCs/DMRs and which particular exon they are overlapping. I think easiest way to deal with this is to add row numbers to transcript ids (if you are confident with your transcripts). Adding row numbers to only repeated ids would be more tricky to program.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
Hi Raza,

I am assuming that this data belongs to WGBS (For RRBS we do not deduplicate) and the genome is mm10.

The aligned sequences after deduplication are in the range of 43M-73M. This is a very low number of reads for WGBS. I do not expect much coverage in this data. So, this could be the reason for failure. Also, it would have been more informative if details of the experiment ie., if this data is single end or paired end and the read length.

mm10 is ~700MB. Which means one would need close to two lanes of HiSeq 2500 ie., ~ 360M PE 100bp data for 10X coverage of the genome (Consider the duplication in data and overlap in paired reads). Based on this information you may estimate what else you need!

Regards,
Kalyan

>

>

>
> From Altuna:  "I think the problem is in the file structure. Usually, Column 11 and 12 of the bed file contains the blockSizes and blockStarts which denote the start and length of each exon. What is out of ordinary about that file is that for "-" strand blockStarts do not start with 0 and the order of the start positions in the blockStarts column is reversed. Below is  an example. Where column 11 and column 12 is reversed for "-" strand.
>
>
> > ref[ref$V4=="AT5G08160.1",]

>

> 0,659,928,1269,1523,2167
>
> You can pre-process (perl, awk, etc. ) the BED entries on "-" strand and reverse the order of values in column 11 and 12, and then it should work. > Best,

there is no function to get such a table. But methylKit objects are coercible to GRanges objects from GenomicRanges. Using functions from GenomicRanges you can get such a table. I don't have an example code for that though. Altuna

>
>
> 1) Which is the difference between table 1 and table 2? I noticed that numbers in Table 2 add up to 100% but in Table 1 does not.
> I guess that table 1 is saying that 52% of my DM-CpGs are located in regions of the genome annotated as promoter. But since exon1 many times overlap promoters, then their must be a number of DM-CpGs that are counted in both columumn (promoter, exons). The number of DM-CpGs overlapping exons and introns is smaller in table 2. I do not understand that difference. Can someone explain? Is there any post or documentation where this is explained more in detail? By searching with :
> "percentage of target features overlapping with annotation (with promoter>exon>intron precedence)", only 3 post are retrieved and non of them explain my question.
>

precedence version gives precedence to promoter overlaps over other overlaps, exon overlaps over intron overlaps. if a CpG is overlapping with a promoter of a gene and also exon/intron, it is counted as promoter overlapping. Without, precedence CpGs can be overlapping with features of different genes at the same time. A CpG may be in a promoter of a transcript/gene but also on the exon of another

> 2) which is the lengh of an annotation boundarie? one base? do these means that 25% of the DM-CpGs fall just in that base? I do not think so but I do not know how a boundary is defined here. Can someone explain?
>
>

Table 3 reverses the question. What percent of promoters,exons or introns overlap with DM-CpGs? The other tables are looking at what percent of DM-CpGs overlap with annotation. Annotation boundary = genomic features such as promoter,exon and intron.

Best,
Altuna

We‘ve been using methylkit to analysis RRBS data and it works quite nicely.
Recently we got data from another kind of experiment and below is the data format. It's a tag-based experiment and the count number (integer) in the fifth column is related to the modification level. This the only value for each position. We want to treat it similarly as RRBS data and analysis using methylkit, maybe with slight modification. Do you think this is possible? Thanks for the help.

chr start stop strand count
chr5 125269917 125269918 - 44
chr2 115966567 115966568 + 5
chr2 3918498 3918499 - 30
chr4 139081349 139081350 + 12
chr9 71788982 71788983 + 31
chr3 58908580 58908581 + 12
chr8 76562031 76562032 + 7

Best,

Jason

messages.body_plain:
Hi Altuna,

I can confirm that tileMethylCounts() works with the example data that comes with your package (test1.myCpG.txt, test2.myCpG.txt, ...). Hence it seems to be an issue of my data or at least my data triggers something...

My Methylbase object 'meth' was generated from BSMAP/methratio output as follows( 6 samples in total; 2 conditions with 3 replicates each):

my_meth_obj=read(file.list,sample.id <http://sample.id>=as.list(sample_ids),treatment=my_treatment,assembly="mm10",header=TRUE, context="CpG", resolution="base",pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,start.col=2,end.col=2,strand.col=3,freqC.col=5,coverage.col=6 ))

# remove entries with zero coverage
for(i in 1:num_samples){
      print(paste("Removing NAs resulting from zero coverage from sample:",sample_ids[[i]],sep=" "))
      my_meth_obj[[i]]=my_meth_obj[[i]][!is.na <http://is.na>(my_meth_obj[[i]]$numCs/my_meth_obj[[i]]$coverage),]
}

# Filtering
filtered.my_meth_obj=filterByCoverage(my_meth_obj,lo.count=7,lo.perc=NULL,hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

#Merge samples
meth=unite(filtered.my_meth_obj,destrand=TRUE,min.per.group=3)

tiles=tileMethylCounts(meth,win.size=1000,step.size=1000)

Error: 'levels' is not an exported object from 'namespace:IRanges'

Any idea howto investigate this further? Unfortunately the original data set is too large for a reproducible example. Maybe I can break it down to a reasonable size for an example.

Best regards,
Michael

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am assuming that tag based method involves sequencing (since this is single nucleotide resolution data). In such a case, the modification level calculation might involve the counts of methylated and unmethylated counts. So, if one could track back to the file with such counts, it would be possible to integrate this data into methylKit.

If the data could not be traced back, Altuna suggestion may be the way to go!

Regards,
Kalyan

Dear Altuna
Same as Jason Liao I'm concern when I annotate differentially methylated CpGs  in this way (assign a gene name by the distance to the nearest TSS). We usually annotate CpGs with gene names to prepare the data set for further analysis (i.e. gene ontology). And we usually assume that the differential methylation is some how affecting that gene (the one we linked to the DM-CpG). However there are plenty of evidence that methylation in promoters  and methylation in exons  have different consequences in the activity of a gene.
It is any way to annotate DM-CpG following a precedence rule ( one that give exons priority during the annotation)?
Txs.
Ale

messages.body_plain:
There might be cases where distance to nearest TSS is shorter to the TSS of adjacent gene for an exonic DMC.

You get an annotation matrix see getMembers() function. That matrix contains the TRUE/FALSE or (0/1) values for a DMC overlapping with promoter/exon/intron. you can come up with your own precedence rule using that matrix.

Best,
Altuna

The possible issues in the SAM file could be any/all of the following:
Presence of header line. Lines that start with "@"
The chromosme names are not in the format "Chr"
SAM is either sorted using SAMTOOLS or PICARD and not with unix "sort". I am saying this because the first alignment in your data is somewhere after 4 million bases and the next alignment is after 33 million bases
It is also possible that the issue is somewhere else. But I would atleast start by sorting these issues first!

Regards,
Kalyan

  scan() expected 'an integer', got '33.3333'

After trying to find out the problem, I noticed that after 200 lines there is a CpG with freqC =33.33.

chr1.771963     chr1    771963  R       3       33.3333 66.6667

Actually it should not be a problem. Somehow methylKit didn't accept 'real number' in this case. It seems that methylKit derives the class information for each column of the data by reading few lines at the beginning and assumes that every entry follows the same pattern. Here in my case the first few lines are integers and real numbers come later. This seems to result in error (I rectified this by replacing an integer with a 'real number' in the first CpG of the file, then it worked)

How about defining the class information while performing scan() rather than allowing methylkit to assess class?

Regards,
Kalyan

if you add ".0" on the to the fist row and fregC and fregT columns, the function will correctly think those are numeric values, since the function reads first couple of hundred lines and decides classes,
alternatively you can try the new mread() function I'm working on. It is faster and doesn't have this problem, https://gist.github.com/al2na/6e47cf0a084ecfbd3075

# load the mread function and methylKit
library(methylKit)
library(devtools)
source_gist("6e47cf0a084ecfbd3075")

file.list=list( system.file("extdata", "test1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "test2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
                system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit") )

# read the files to a methylRawList object: myobj
myobj=mread( file.list,
            sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2"),assembly="hg18",treatment=c(1,1,0,0))

myobj2=mread( file.list[[1]],sample.id <http://sample.id>="test1",assembly="hg18")

Usage is similar to the read() function:

mread(location,sample.id <http://sample.id>,assembly,pipeline="amp",header=T,skip=0,sep="\t",context="CpG",resolution="base",treatment)
